author: Jackson Lilly
title: Toxicology report released in Kanawha County ambulance death case - NewsBreak
text:
By Jackson Lilly ,
11 hours ago
EDITOR'S NOTE: This story has been updated with the latest information. The video attached to this story is from our previous coverage.
KANAWHA COUNTY, W.Va. (WOWK) - A motion has been made to approve an expert witness in the case against a former Kanawha County ambulance driver.
According to the motion, Alyssa Middleton is requesting the court to approve a forensic toxicologist as an expert witness.
This is in response to the release of the toxicology report for John Lucas.
The toxicology report alleges that the victim's blood reflects a level of methamphetamine and caffeine in the victim's system.
The defense claims that expert testimony from a forensic toxicologist is required to interpret toxicological concepts to the jury and how those concepts apply to this case.
A statement released from the counsel for the family of John Lucas states in part, "The release of John Curtis Lucas’s toxicology report does not change the facts that are at the heart of this case. The report indicates that John had methamphetamine and caffeine in his system at the time of his death. That information does not excuse what happened to him, nor does it answer the critical questions surrounding his death." said the Summers Law Office, PLLC. "The issue is not whether John had methamphetamine in his system. The issue is what happened when the ambulance encountered him in the roadway and what the occupants of that ambulance did afterward."
Alyssa Middleton has pleaded not guilty to charges of voluntary manslaughter, aggravated vehicular homicide, and leaving the scene of an accident causing death, all felonies.
The charges stem from the April 16 death of John Lucas in Elkview , who was struck and killed by the ambulance allegedly driven by Middleton. On the day of the incident, deputies said the EMTs claimed they believed Lucas was holding a knife.
